# AI Model Explorer

> Free, open-source (MIT) web tool by Sattaya Singkul that splits any AI model architecture into its parts and shows the real weights, compute, TFLite op count and precision of each part. Thai and English. https://joessattes.github.io/ai-model-explorer/

AI Model Explorer reads a model from three kinds of input and works out its anatomy automatically:

- a `.tflite` (LiteRT) file — the real op graph is parsed in the browser (ops, tensor shapes, dtypes, quantize/dequantize "seams");
- a Hugging Face repository — only the safetensors header is read (tensor names, shapes, dtypes; no weights downloaded);
- a pasted `config.json` — the structure is synthesized for common families (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi, GPT-2, BERT, RoBERTa, ViT, Whisper, BART, T5).

It recognises encoder–decoder (e.g. Whisper), decoder-only LLMs (e.g. Llama, GPT-2, Qwen) and encoder-only models (e.g. BERT, ViT), for text, audio and image.

## What it shows
- Big picture: the model as numbered parts (input → embedding → encoder/decoder stacks → output head), with a play-through that shows each part's input and output, a zoom into one layer, and the decoder's per-token loop.
- Lenses: weights (bytes, params), compute (FLOPs), TFLite op count, precision (fp32/fp16/bf16/int8/int4), fragility (output error when one part is quantized to int4, where measured).
- Layer map drawn to scale, including weight bytes read per input (the decoder re-reads its weights every token).
- Concepts with numbers from the selected model (attention, feed-forward, KV cache, tied embedding, seams) and a quantization playground.
- Report with insights and a Markdown table to copy.

## Templates included
- biodatlab/distill-whisper-th-medium (Thai speech recognition) — real .tflite graph of the architecture, 1,616 ops
- meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B, openai-community/gpt2, google-bert/bert-base-uncased, google/vit-base-patch16-224 — structure from the transformers implementation
- Whisper rehearsal models in fp32, weight-only int8 and dynamic int4 for precision comparisons
